keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «우리가 즐기는 많은 음식이 꽃가루받이에 달려 있다(주제)» 와 «벌을 지키는 것은 곧 우리 식탁의 음식을 지키는 일이다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (many of the foods we enjoy depend on pollination) and the conclusion (protecting bees is about protecting the food on our tables). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why are honeybee hives trucked into almond orchards in California every spring?
qs.qko: 캘리포니아에서는 왜 해마다 봄이면 꿀벌 벌통을 아몬드 과수원으로 실어 나르나요?
opts: Without the bees, the almond harvest would be much smaller
The bees make the almonds taste sweeter
Farmers want to sell the hives to tourists
evs: Without them, the harvest would be much smaller.
Some plants, such as wheat and rice, are pollinated mainly by the wind.
Beekeepers in many countries have reported large losses of colonies in recent decades.
Fortunately, there are ways to help.
why: 본문에 벌이 없으면 수확량이 훨씬 적어질 것이라고 나와요. 아몬드 꽃의 꽃가루받이를 벌이 해 주기 때문이에요.
The text says that without the bees, the harvest would be much smaller.

qs.q: In the text, what does "honeybees are only part of the story" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «honeybees are only part of the story» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Many other insects, such as wild bees and butterflies, also pollinate crops
Honeybees only work during part of the year
Only half of all honeybees can make honey
evs: Thousands of species of wild bees, along with butterflies, flies, and other insects, also pollinate crops, and some are even more efficient than honeybees.
In California, for example, huge numbers of honeybee hives are trucked into almond orchards every spring.
Some plants, such as wheat and rice, are pollinated mainly by the wind.
Beekeepers in many countries have reported large losses of colonies in recent decades.
why: 바로 다음 문장에서 수천 종의 야생벌과 나비, 파리 같은 다른 곤충도 작물의 꽃가루받이를 한다고 해요. 꿀벌은 이야기의 일부일 뿐이라는 뜻이에요.
The next sentence says thousands of species of wild bees, butterflies, and flies also pollinate crops. Honeybees are only one part.

qs.q: How do bees help pollen travel from one flower to another?
qs.qko: 벌은 꽃가루가 한 꽃에서 다른 꽃으로 옮겨 가도록 어떻게 돕나요?
opts: Pollen sticks to bees' hairy bodies as they collect nectar and is carried to the next flower
Bees eat the pollen and drop seeds on the ground
Bees fan their wings so the wind blows pollen into the sky
evs: Pollination is the movement of pollen from one flower to another, which allows plants to produce fruit and seeds.
As bees collect nectar for food, pollen sticks to their hairy bodies and travels to the next flower.
Some plants, such as wheat and rice, are pollinated mainly by the wind.
Scientists point to several causes working together, including the loss of wild flowers, certain pesticides, parasites like the varroa mite, diseases, and climate change.
why: 꽃가루받이는 꽃가루가 한 꽃에서 다른 꽃으로 옮겨 가 열매와 씨를 맺게 하는 일이에요. 벌이 꽃꿀을 모을 때 털 많은 몸에 꽃가루가 붙어 다음 꽃으로 옮겨져요. 두 문장을 이어 봐야 해요.
Pollination is the movement of pollen between flowers. As bees collect nectar, pollen sticks to their hairy bodies and travels to the next flower.

ends: How do beekeepers take care of their hives?
Which flowers help wild bees the most?
